claim: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology is conducting replications of 50 papers in the field of cancer biology published between 2010 and 2012.
source: The Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology seeks to address growing concerns about reproducibility in scientific research by conducting replications of 50 papers in the field of cancer biology published between 2010 and 2012.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a description of the project scope.

claim: Lin et al. (2012) published 'Transcriptional amplification in tumor cells with elevated c-Myc' in Cell in 2012.
source: This Registered report describes the proposed replication plan of key experiments from 'Transcriptional amplification in tumor cells with elevated c-Myc' by Lin et al. (2012), published in Cell in 2012.
evidence: This is a direct citation to the original publication being replicated.

claim: Elevated levels of c-Myc in the P493-6 cell model of Burkitt's lymphoma results in an increase of the total level of RNA using UV/VIS spectrophotometry.
source: In these experiments, elevated levels of c-Myc in the P493-6 cell model of Burkitt's lymphoma results in an increase of the total level of RNA using UV/VIS spectrophotometry (Figure 3E; Lin et al., 2012)
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3E from Lin et al., 2012.

claim: Elevated c-Myc increases mRNA levels/cell for a large set of genes using digital gene expression technology.
source: elevated levels of c-Myc in the P493-6 cell model of Burkitt's lymphoma results in an increase of the total level of RNA using UV/VIS spectrophotometry (Figure 3E; Lin et al., 2012) and on the mRNA levels/cell for a large set of genes using digital gene expression technology (Figure 3F; Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by reference to Figure 3F from Lin et al., 2012.

claim: The proto-oncogene MYC is frequently amplified in human cancers.
source: The proto-oncogene MYC is frequently amplified in human cancers and encodes the transcription factor c-Myc, which is associated with a variety of cellular processes such as cell growth and proliferation (Dang, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dang, 2013.

claim: MYC encodes the transcription factor c-Myc.
source: The proto-oncogene MYC is frequently amplified in human cancers and encodes the transcription factor c-Myc, which is associated with a variety of cellular processes such as cell growth and proliferation (Dang, 2013).
evidence: This is established biological knowledge cited to Dang, 2013.

claim: c-Myc is associated with a variety of cellular processes such as cell growth and proliferation.
source: The proto-oncogene MYC is frequently amplified in human cancers and encodes the transcription factor c-Myc, which is associated with a variety of cellular processes such as cell growth and proliferation (Dang, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Dang, 2013.

claim: Overexpressed c-Myc is known to contribute to tumorigenesis.
source: While overexpressed c-Myc is known to contribute to tumorigenesis, an understanding of how this process occurs is complicated by a number of issues, including the large number of binding sites and the diversity between systems.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the field.

claim: Lin et al. (2012) present findings that c-Myc functions by globally amplifying the expression of actively transcribed genes.
source: While this was thought to occur by regulation of a specific subset of genes, Lin et al. (2012) present findings that c-Myc functions by globally amplifying the expression of actively transcribed genes.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the findings from Lin et al., 2012.

claim: The P493-6 human B cell model of Burkitt's lymphoma contains a tetracycline-repressible MYC transgene.
source: The system used is the human P493-6 B cell model of Burkitt's lymphoma, which contains a tetracycline-repressible MYC transgene, allowing for titration of c-Myc protein (Schuhmacher et al., 1999; Pajic et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schuhmacher et al., 1999 and Pajic et al., 2000.

claim: The tetracycline-repressible MYC transgene in P493-6 cells allows for titration of c-Myc protein.
source: The system used is the human P493-6 B cell model of Burkitt's lymphoma, which contains a tetracycline-repressible MYC transgene, allowing for titration of c-Myc protein (Schuhmacher et al., 1999; Pajic et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schuhmacher et al., 1999 and Pajic et al., 2000.

claim: The levels of c-Myc can be reduced and subsequently re-induced in a gradual time-dependent manner in P493-6 cells.
source: The levels of c-Myc can be reduced and subsequently re-induced in a gradual time-dependent manner, as determined by western blot, which is shown in Figure 1B (Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by reference to Figure 1B from Lin et al., 2012.

claim: As soon as 1 hr after re-induction, the protein levels of c-Myc increased above the repressed levels.
source: As soon as 1 hr after re-induction, the protein levels of c-Myc increased above the repressed levels, which by 24 hr were similar to the tetracycline-free condition (Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a finding from Lin et al., 2012.

claim: By 24 hr after re-induction, c-Myc protein levels were similar to the tetracycline-free condition.
source: As soon as 1 hr after re-induction, the protein levels of c-Myc increased above the repressed levels, which by 24 hr were similar to the tetracycline-free condition (Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a finding from Lin et al., 2012.

claim: The P493-6 system has been used in other studies with similar results observed.
source: This system has been used in other studies with similar results observed (Schuhmacher et al., 1999; Pajic et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Schuhmacher et al., 1999 and Pajic et al., 2000.

claim: Lin et al. (2012) reported an increase in levels of absolute RNA over the timecourse of c-Myc re-induction in P493-6 cells.
source: Lin et al. (2012) reported an increase in levels of absolute RNA over the timecourse of c-Myc re-induction.
evidence: This is a direct statement about findings from Lin et al., 2012.

claim: c-Myc increases RNA content per cell.
source: This experiment shows that c-Myc increases RNA content per cell, indicating c-Myc functions primarily in transcriptional amplification.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results from Lin et al., 2012.

claim: c-Myc functions primarily in transcriptional amplification.
source: This experiment shows that c-Myc increases RNA content per cell, indicating c-Myc functions primarily in transcriptional amplification.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental results.

claim: Related experiments using mouse B cells observed the same c-Myc-dependent amplification of cellular RNA content.
source: Related experiments, using mouse B cells, also observed the same c-Myc-dependent amplification of cellular RNA content (Nie et al., 2012; Sabò et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Nie et al., 2012 and Sabò et al., 2014.

claim: Similar experiments in 3T9 fibroblasts or U2OS cells expressing an inducible c-Myc did not observe an increase in cellular RNA content.
source: However, similar experiments in 3T9 fibroblasts or U2OS cells expressing an inducible c-Myc did not observe an increase in cellular RNA content (Sabò et al., 2014; Walz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sabò et al., 2014 and Walz et al., 2014.

claim: An increase in total cellular RNA content was observed in 3T9 fibroblasts following serum stimulation.
source: Interestingly, an increase in total cellular RNA content was observed in 3T9 fibroblasts following serum stimulation, which was not observed when c-Myc was deleted in these cells (Sabò et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sabò et al., 2014.

claim: The increase in total cellular RNA content following serum stimulation in 3T9 fibroblasts was not observed when c-Myc was deleted in these cells.
source: Interestingly, an increase in total cellular RNA content was observed in 3T9 fibroblasts following serum stimulation, which was not observed when c-Myc was deleted in these cells (Sabò et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sabò et al., 2014.

claim: Re-induction of c-Myc increased the number of active genes (defined as greater than 1 transcript/cell).
source: Re-induction of c-Myc increased the number of active genes (defined as greater than 1 transcript/cell), but did not alter silent genes (defined as less than 0.5 transcript/cell) (Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a finding from Lin et al., 2012.

claim: Re-induction of c-Myc did not alter silent genes (defined as less than 0.5 transcript/cell).
source: Re-induction of c-Myc increased the number of active genes (defined as greater than 1 transcript/cell), but did not alter silent genes (defined as less than 0.5 transcript/cell) (Lin et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a finding from Lin et al., 2012.

claim: Elevated c-Myc levels lead to an amplification of the existing transcriptional profile.
source: This key finding suggests that elevated c-Myc levels lead to an amplification of the existing transcriptional profile.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings from Lin et al., 2012.

claim: An increase in transcription of c-Myc target genes was observed in mouse B cells treated with the Myc-Max dimerization inhibitor 10058-F4 and analyzed by ChIP-Seq.
source: This finding was observed in other experiments using mouse B cells treated with the Myc-Max dimerization inhibitor 10058-F4 and analyzed by ChIP-Seq (Nie et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Nie et al., 2012.

claim: P493-6 cells showed an increase in transcription of c-Myc target genes when c-Myc re-induction was titrated to different concentrations by microarray analysis.
source: Another report using P493-6 cells also found an increase in transcription of c-Myc target genes when c-Myc re-induction was titrated to different concentrations by microarray analysis (Schuhmacher and Eick, 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schuhmacher and Eick, 2013.

claim: RNA amplification and promoter/enhancer invasion by c-Myc were separable events in 3T9 fibroblasts and U2OS cells.
source: These studies found that RNA amplification and promoter/enhancer invasion by c-Myc were separable events in 3T9 fibroblasts and U2OS cells, suggesting that c-Myc regulates a distinct subset of genes, which indirectly lead to RNA amplification (Sabò et al., 2014; Walz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Sabò et al., 2014 and Walz et al., 2014.

claim: c-Myc regulates a distinct subset of genes, which indirectly lead to RNA amplification.
source: These studies found that RNA amplification and promoter/enhancer invasion by c-Myc were separable events in 3T9 fibroblasts and U2OS cells, suggesting that c-Myc regulates a distinct subset of genes, which indirectly lead to RNA amplification (Sabò et al., 2014; Walz et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an interpretation from studies cited as Sabò et al., 2014 and Walz et al., 2014.

claim: Serum has been reported to stimulate the expression of a majority of genes independently from c-Myc.
source: One major variable in this system is serum, which has been reported to stimulate the expression of a majority of genes independently from c-Myc (Schlosser et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Schlosser et al., 2005.

claim: The replication will use two separate lots of serum to assess if there is variability between different batches of serum.
source: P493-6 cells will be cultured with two separate lots of serum that will be maintained throughout all the experiments to assess if there is variability between different batches of serum.
evidence: This is stated as part of the experimental design.

claim: The original study used three separate custom code sets (CS-1, CS-2, and CS-MYC) with a total of 495 genes, of which only 479 were unique.
source: The original study used three separate custom code sets (CS-1, CS-2, and CS-MYC) and the replication will combine these into one custom code set. The three original custom code sets had a total of 495 genes, of which only 479 were unique, so the replication custom code set will only contain these unique genes.
evidence: This is stated as a known difference from the original study.

claim: The nCounter GX human immunology kit from NanoString has been updated to a new version with 106 new genes not present in the first version, of which 101 are unique to all genes examined in this experiment.
source: The nCounter GX human immunology kit from NanoString has been updated to a new version. In the second version, there are 106 new genes not present in the first version, of which 101 are unique to all genes examined in this experiment, while 38 genes that were in the first version are excluded in the second version.
evidence: This is stated as a known difference from the original study.

claim: 63 unique genes will be added to the total gene set compared with the original study changing the total examined genes from 1346 to 1409.
source: Thus, 63 unique genes will be added to the total gene set compared with the original study changing the total examined genes from 1346 to 1409.
evidence: This is stated as a known difference from the original study.

claim: The original study analyzed data using the Wilcoxon sum rank test.
source: The original study analyzed these data using the Wilcoxon sum rank test, however since expressions of the same gene across different conditions are not independent, the Wilcoxon signed rank test, a non-parametric test for comparing two paired samples, will be used instead.
evidence: This is stated as a known difference from the original study.

claim: The replication will use the Wilcoxon signed rank test because expressions of the same gene across different conditions are not independent.
source: The original study analyzed these data using the Wilcoxon sum rank test, however since expressions of the same gene across different conditions are not independent, the Wilcoxon signed rank test, a non-parametric test for comparing two paired samples, will be used instead.
evidence: This is stated as a methodological decision based on statistical reasoning.
